title: U.S. House · California's 50th District
area: Coastal and central San Diego, including the City of San Diego and nearby communities.

context.text: The district's boundaries changed as a result of California Proposition 50, a mid-decade congressional redistricting measure voters approved on November 4, 2025.

Incumbent Scott Peters and Steve Cohen advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary. Peters won 48.1% of the primary vote (102,057 votes) and Cohen won 39.8% (84,340 votes); other candidates included Aishwarya Mitra, Tim Arnous, Joseph Shea and Lucinda Jahn.

candidates.name: Scott Peters
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 48.1% of the vote.

summary.text: Scott Peters is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative, first elected to Congress in 2012. He previously served on the San Diego City Council from 2000 to 2008, including as council president from 2006 to 2008, and worked as an economist for the Environmental Protection Agency and as an attorney.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in political science and economics from Duke University in 1980 and a J.D. from New York University School of Law in 1984.
Worked as an economist for the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and as an attorney before entering politics.
Served on the San Diego City Council from 2000 to 2008, serving as council president from 2006 to 2008.

priorities.text: Making health care more accessible and affordable for families, including lowering out-of-pocket costs.
priorities.quote: We need to make health care more accessible and affordable for families.

priorities.text: Growing San Diego's economy by investing in innovation, small businesses and job creation while containing inflation.
priorities.quote: Congress must keep investing in programs that grow our economy, contain inflation, and create jobs.

priorities.text: Firearm safety reform, prioritized as a member of the Congressional Gun Violence Prevention Task Force.

positions.summary: Says all women deserve equal access to reproductive health care without government interference and is a member of the Congressional Pro-Choice Caucus; has cosponsored the Women's Health Protection Act.
positions.quote: Scott believes that all women deserve equal access to reproductive health care without interference from the government.

positions.summary: Calls for universal background checks, banning weapons of war, and prohibiting suspected terrorists and domestic abusers from purchasing firearms; a member of the Congressional Gun Violence Prevention Task Force.
positions.quote: Congress can prevent these tragedies if it implements universal background checks, bans weapons of war, and prohibits suspected terrorists and domestic abusers from purchasing firearms.

positions.summary: Says the country must rapidly reduce greenhouse gas emissions to address climate change and has introduced bills aimed at cutting emissions while building clean energy.
positions.quote: To protect San Diegans and the nation from the worst consequences of climate change, we must rapidly reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

positions.summary: Says San Diego needs to build more housing for people of all income levels and is working to incentivize more housing development.
positions.quote: We need to build more housing for people of all income levels in a way that’s thoughtfully planned for our communities.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (Communications and Technology, Energy, and Environment subcommittees) and the House Committee on Budget for the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Served on the Joint Economic Committee during the 117th Congress (2021-2022) in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce and Committee on Budget.

candidates.researchNotes: Peters has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, but his official House website's issue pages (scottpeters.house.gov/issues/...) were reachable and provided sourced priorities and positions.

candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 39.8% of the vote.
